newsitem.title: UK: Cellnet to start roaming in U.S.
newsitem.headline: Cellnet to start roaming in U.S.

text.p: Cellnet, the UK mobile telephones group 60 percent owned by British Telecommunications, said on Thursday its customers would be able to use their existing phone numbers and accounts in 50 U.S. states and Canada from 1997.
"Cellnet is set to become the first UK mobile phone network to offer its digital users a service throughout the United States and Canada," it said in a statement.

But because of differences in technology between U.S. and UK mobile telephone networks, Cellnet customers will only be able to use the "GlobalRoam" service if they buy, or rent U.S. mobile phones -- or American Mobile Phone Systems (AMPS).
These phones, which use the older analogue network, cost from around 175 stg to buy or from 49 stg per week to hire.

Cellnet, which has sealed roaming agreements with 75 networks covering 52 countries worldwide, also announced that from early 1997, digital customers would be able to use the newer digital network in Washington DC and Baltimore.

Until the birth of multi-band handsets, allowing customers to switch to any frequency using one mobile phone, travellers will need to use a U.S. digital phone which costs around 400 stg To buy or 49 stg per week to rent for this service.
